items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: Gershwin was there... amongst other nobility of the music world... Gershwin heard Lew Leslie make that remark... Gershwin would explain to him [Joe Steele] just what was what

ctx.x: Now, you said at one time that he played "Rhapsody in Blue" for Gershwin.

Well, they were putting on a show. "Rhapsody In Black" was the name of the show. An all-Negro show. And Gershwin provided the music. So they were using Gershwin's "Rhapsody In Blue" in the show. Now, this goes way back to the early Twenties, and "Rhapsody In Blue" at that time was not so popular -- it was just beginning to get known.

So they sent for Joe Steele to make an audition to play the Rhapsody to be used in the show, and Gershwin was there, amongst other nobility of the music world. So Joe comes in and he sits at the piano, and the conductor gives him the go-ahead signal. So the band started off, and Joe sits at the piano -- and he went all through the Rhapsody, beginning to end. And when they got through, Joe got a big hand from all the commentators standing around, musicians and one thing or another.
